endpoints.payer: Bucket owner. Every request was unsigned, so no requester was charged.

definitions.acquisition: A distinct sensing date and platform letter on one tile, as in the gap survey. An aquatic reflectance acquisition takes both from the object name.
definitions.earth_search_any: Acquisitions in any of the three Earth Search collections.
definitions.latency: Hours from the sensing start in the object name to the earliest last-modified time of the scene's objects. It describes the bucket copy.
definitions.join: Tile, platform, and sensing start from the product names. Exact when the processing baseline also agrees. Collection 1 first, then the older collection.
definitions.cloud_cover: Earth Search Level-1C eo:cloud_cover per acquisition, the lowest of its items, split by whether the acquisition has a product scene.
definitions.l1c: same_product: Earth Search's Level-1C collection lists the Level-1C product named in the aquatic reflectance object name. same_pass_other_product: it lists the pass with another baseline or generation time. no_pass: neither.

limitations: Listings and catalog metadata only. No object body and no pixel was read, so listed scenes are not shown to open or to hold valid water pixels.
Earth Search is the reference. Its own completeness against ESA is measured separately in the gap survey, and only from 2021.
Acquisition keys pair date and platform. Two passes of one unit on one tile and date would collapse into one key.
Object last-modified times describe when the bucket copy was written. They can postdate processing, and a rewritten object resets its time.
Recent latency covers scenes sensed in the last 120 days of the window. Scenes not yet published are absent, so the statistic is biased low.
Tiles outside the lower 48 get one listing page each. A presence count, not a survey.
Counts describe the bucket and the catalog at measured_at.
